Case_20004/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1A. Image of the patient’s leg demonstrating skin lesions with sporotrichoid pattern before treatment with voriconazole.

description.short_caption: Skin lesions with sporotrichoid pattern on the leg.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the anterior aspect of a leg with multiple erythematous, ulcerated nodules arranged in a linear pattern, consistent with a sporotrichoid distribution. The lesions appear to vary in size and severity, with some showing central ulceration and crusting. The surrounding skin shows mild erythema and discoloration. The image is well-lit, and the lesions are clearly visible.

Case_20004/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2B. Representative histopathology from the skin biopsy. A fungus is discernible on periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain (40x magnification)

description.short_caption: Histopathology of skin biopsy showing fungal elements on PAS stain (40x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a skin biopsy stained with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain at 40x magnification. The tissue demonstrates fungal elements, which appear as magenta-stained structures against a pink and purple background. The fungal morphology is consistent with hyphae or yeast forms, suggesting a fungal infection. The surrounding tissue shows some degree of inflammation and cellular debris.

Case_20004/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2A. Representative histopathology from the skin biopsy. Hematoxylin and eosin staining demonstrates a focus of necrotizing neutrophilic and granulomatous inflammation at the base of the biopsy (20x magnification)

description.short_caption: H&E stain showing necrotizing neutrophilic and granulomatous inflammation in a skin biopsy (20x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), demonstrates a focus of necrotizing inflammation at the base of a skin biopsy. The inflammatory infiltrate includes neutrophils and granulomatous components, with areas of necrosis visible as pale, acellular regions. The magnification is approximately 20x, providing a detailed view of the cellular architecture and inflammatory changes.

Case_20004/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2D. Representative histopathology from the skin biopsy. Grocott Methenamine Silver (GMS) stain with the fungus appearing as irregular septated hyphae and yeast forms (100x magnification)

description.short_caption: GMS-stained skin biopsy showing irregular septated hyphae and yeast forms.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a Grocott Methenamine Silver (GMS) stain of a skin biopsy at 100x magnification. The fungal elements are highlighted in black, appearing as irregular septated hyphae and yeast forms against a green background. The staining technique enhances the visualization of fungal structures, aiding in the identification of fungal pathogens.
visible_findings: GMS stain with black fungal elements

Case_20004/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2C. Representative histopathology from the skin biopsy showing PAS stain at 100x magnification

description.short_caption: PAS stain of skin biopsy at 100x magnification showing fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain of a skin biopsy at 100x magnification. The field contains numerous fungal elements, including yeast forms and pseudohyphae, which are highlighted in magenta against a pale background. The surrounding tissue shows evidence of inflammation and cellular debris. The PAS stain is used to identify polysaccharides in fungal cell walls, making fungal elements stand out distinctly.
visible_findings: background of inflamed tissue and cellular debris

Case_20004/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1B. Image of the patient’s leg with resolved skin lesions after treatment with voriconazole.

description.short_caption: Clinical photograph of the leg showing partially healed skin lesions.
description.detailed_description: This image shows the anterior aspect of a leg with multiple partially healed skin lesions. The lesions are circular to oval, with central crusting and surrounding hyperpigmentation. There is evidence of healing, as some lesions appear less inflamed and more pigmented compared to active lesions. The surrounding skin shows mild discoloration, likely post-inflammatory changes.
